business: MYTHRI (AI Emotional Support & Mental Health Companion)
target: Adults 18 to 35 seeking accessible emotional support, coping tools, and a safe space to vent between or instead of therapy

behaviours.name: Therapy-priced-out
behaviours.how: Wants professional therapy but cannot afford $120-$200/session or is stuck on long clinic waitlists.

behaviours.name: Late-night venter
behaviours.how: Experiences anxiety or loneliness late at night and needs immediate, non-judgmental conversational grounding.

behaviours.name: Self-care app switcher
behaviours.how: Has tried Calm, Headspace, or journaling apps, but finds one-way meditation tracks too passive and uninvolved.

behaviours.name: Privacy skeptic
behaviours.how: Extremely cautious about where their personal vulnerabilities and chat logs are stored.

behaviours.name: Deal & trial seeker
behaviours.how: Signs up for 7-day trials, evaluates aggressively, and cancels unless value is immediately obvious.

behaviours.name: Reddit / review researcher
behaviours.how: Checks Reddit threads and app store 1-star reviews before entering credit card information.

objections: AI can't replace a real human therapist who actually cares
$9.99/month is steep for what might just be a glorified chatbot
I worry my sensitive mental health logs will be leaked or used to train public models
I always abandon self-care apps after 4 days anyway
What if it hallucinates, gives superficial advice, or doesn't understand my distress?
Free ChatGPT or Claude can already chat with me for free
habits: you scroll social media late at night when you can't sleep
you feel overwhelmed by work deadlines during the day
you have thought about booking therapy but stopped at the price tag
you keep your feelings to yourself because you don't want to burden friends
